events.summary: PKD (age 13) writes home from California Preparatory School in Ojai, defending his decision to stay despite homesickness and refusing his mother's offers to bring him home.
events.evidence_quote: I am not coming home. I have no wish to... I am not that kind of a man, who would run away from something that was difficult to get used to.

events.summary: PKD's English-theme essay on a cat is read aloud to the class by Mr. Barnes after the first paragraph compels it — an early recognition of his prose.
events.evidence_quote: I got 'A' on an English theme which Mr. Barnes read to the class, because they begged him to read it after he had read the first paragraph

events.summary: PKD's mother Dorothy meets with him and urges him to leave his second wife Kleo, offering $600 to fly future-third-wife Anne Rubenstein to Berkeley to meet her.
events.evidence_quote: my mother and I had a long discussion about breaking up a bad marriage (mine, and the one she had with my father). She feels I'd be better off leaving Kleo. She wants to meet you, so here is six hundred dollars to fly back here to meet her at once

events.summary: PKD borrows Anne Rubenstein's station wagon and nearly overheats it driving to a Napa Valley winery with friend Maury; documents his Point Reyes Station / Berkeley shuttling life pre-marriage.
events.evidence_quote: I drove up the freeway toward the Oakland Bay Bridge... There was just enough water left in the radiator to imply that no harm had been done

events.summary: Nancy Hackett (PKD's fourth wife) is approximately one week away from giving birth to their daughter Isa; PKD has logistical plans (cashier's check for $200, cab fare envelope) for the hospital.
events.evidence_quote: Nancy is now about a week away from having the baby... we have planned all manner of clever plans, such as having a cashier's check for $200 ready to give the hospital

events.summary: PKD's beloved cat Horace dies the prior week, evidently from rat-poison ingestion; PKD records it as a foundational loss two years into ownership.
events.evidence_quote: little Horace, the one we loved the most, died last week, evidently from eating rat poison... I only had him with me two years. It was not long enough.

events.summary: PKD's COUNTER-CLOCK WORLD is published by Berkley Books; PKD notes the cover-art girl resembles Nancy and the protagonist Lotta is modeled on her.
events.evidence_quote: My Berkley book, COUNTER-CLOCK WORLD, just came out, with a very nice cover—which shows a girl who looks exactly like Nancy. What is more, the girl in the story, Lotta, is based on Nancy.

events.summary: PKD writes a script for the ABC TV show The Invaders, hopeful Quinn Martin Productions will buy it.
events.evidence_quote: I wrote a script for the TV show, 'The Invaders.' I wonder if they'll buy it (of course they will. It's superb).

events.summary: PKD attends a 'well people' group-therapy session 8pm to 1:30am, with a psychiatrist guiding interpersonal mechanism analysis; Nancy now also attends.
events.evidence_quote: the therapy group which I (and now Nancy) go to? It's for 'well' people, and we act, interact and react, from 8:00 p.m. to 1:30 a.m... The psychiatrist in charge is a good one

events.summary: After Horace's death, PKD buys a four-drawer fireproof file case (700 lbs) and spends days archiving his Unknown and Astounding magazine collection (1933–1943), photographs, letters, manuscripts, and rare Bruno Walter Magic Flute recording.
events.evidence_quote: I went out and bought a huge fire-proof file case (four drawers)... my Astoundings from '33 to '43, all photographs, letters, rare books of poetry, rare tapes (such as Bruno Walter's performance of Mozart's Magic Flute, a copy of each of my books

events.summary: PKD starts a new novel, completes 16 pages, then hits writer's block; blames the new baby Isa and wife Nancy for the disruption.
events.evidence_quote: I started on a new book the other day (for which I've been making notes for four months straight), got 16 good pages done, and then—bam. Nothing.

events.summary: PKD's second cat Johnny disappears after Horace's death and is presumed to have been adopted by another family; PKD's I-Ching consultation reports 'his feet are tied' and 'tender meat'.
events.evidence_quote: Horace's brother Johnny seemed to want to be gone, ever since Horace passed away, and last week Johnny tanked up on food, went out, and never returned... The Oracle says he's alive and living on 'tender meat,'

events.summary: PKD spends a week as voluntary inpatient at OCM Health (Orange County Mental Health) for what staff diagnose as 'future shock' rather than psychiatric illness; intensive group therapy in lieu of medication.
events.evidence_quote: My week in the hospital did a lot for me, emotionally and also intellectually... no medication and no therapy could help me; that my problem was one of human loss and the suffering therefrom: that is future shock personified.

events.summary: PKD records that his marriage with Tessa effectively ended in February 1976; he calls both Tessa and Nancy asking them to take him back, both decline.
events.evidence_quote: As far as my relationship with you goes, I knew in February that it had ended... Besides calling you and asking you if you'd come back to me I called Nancy and asked her the same thing. I got the same answer.

events.summary: PKD signs a Bantam contract for VALISYSTEM A (the alien-satellite plot, working title for what becomes RADIO FREE ALBEMUTH) with a December 1, 1976 manuscript deadline he describes as impossible to meet.
events.evidence_quote: I signed a contract with Bantam and didn't read when I have to have the finished MS to them and then discovered it is this coming December first, a deadline I can't possibly meet (the book is VALISYSTEM A, with the alien satellite plot)

events.summary: PKD is to receive the John W. Campbell Award at a Cal State Fullerton public lecture (per Willis McNelly); the engagement contributes to the stress that lands him in hospital.
events.evidence_quote: McNelly was after me to make a public lecture at CSF at which I would accept the John W. Campbell Award

events.summary: PKD reflects that his fiction is 'an analysis of what makes up a cosmos' and connects this directly to 3-74: 'in 3/74 I got to see the Great Mechanic.'
events.evidence_quote: My books really real with the theme of kosmoi breaking down, and how you fix them; I seem to look at the universe as a sort of used car coasting along and falling apart and being patched together again. It runs, but it always needs some work from the Mechanic.

events.summary: PKD describes his March 1974 experience to ex-wife Nancy in explicitly Christian language: 'an encounter with the Savior which radically changed my life'; current novel VALIS narrates it.
events.evidence_quote: I had a major religious experience back in March of 1974, an encounter with the Savior which radically changed my life. My current novel is an account of that experience

events.summary: PKD begins attending Bible-based Protestant churches within walking distance of his Santa Ana apartment.
events.evidence_quote: There are indeed a number of Bible-based churches based within walking distance of my apartment. I've already gone over to one.

events.summary: VALIS manuscript sells to Bantam for $10,000; DEUS IRAE paperback for $11,500 (US) and $9,000 (UK); PKD owes IRS $4,050 from the resulting income.
events.evidence_quote: VALIS sold for $10,000; and DEUS IRAE sold for (the paperback) a record $11,500. In England DEUS IRAE sold for $9,000, which is more than my agent can get for Norman Mailer's new book

events.summary: PKD's Bantam editor objects that VALIS reads like 'Revelation' and 'you write like you've become a Jesus freak'; PKD refuses to alter the religious content.
events.evidence_quote: 'You write like you've become a Jesus freak,' he said on the phone to me. 'Your new book reads like Revelation.' He wanted me to remove or alter some of the parts because of the religion, but I'm not going to.

events.summary: Sherri Solvig (PKD's neighbor) has inoperable cancer (currently in remission); PKD reveals her illness was a main factor in his decision to leave Tessa, that she lives in the apartment next to his, and that they share dinner nightly.
events.evidence_quote: she has inoperable cancer, and this was a main factor in my decision to leave Tessa and live with her; Sherri was alone and sick with no one to take care of her... My doctor says she would be dead by now except for me.

events.summary: PKD is hospitalized in February 1976 (separate episode from the October hospitalization); Sherri visits him almost daily.
events.evidence_quote: When I was in the hospital back in February, it was Sherri who came to see me almost every day and to take care of me.
